Metadata.Summary: DermGPT is an AI chatbot developed by Faranak Kamangar, MD, designed to streamline clinical tasks, improve access to dermatologic data, and save time for physicians. It is built on more than 3,000 peer-reviewed articles and aims to improve clinical efficiency. DermGPT is free for dermatologists to use.
Metadata.Keywords: AI; artificial intelligence; dermatology; chatbot; clinical efficiency; peer-reviewed; prior authorization; patient education; diagnosis; treatment; prescription programs; medication options; telehealth

UsesAndDirections.IntendedUseAndWorkflow: DermGPT is intended to assist dermatologists and their staff with various tasks, including looking up dermatology information (diagnoses, treatments, prior authorization criteria), patient management, shared decision-making (patient educational handouts, prescription programs), answering patient inquiries, providing quick references for medication options, summarizing diagnosis and treatment guidelines, suggesting labs/imaging/procedures, automating documentation (visit notes, orders, prescriptions), writing insurance authorization letters, creating patient handouts, summarizing medical notes, assisting with study guides for board exams, and providing informed consent language.
UsesAndDirections.PrimaryIntendedUsers: Dermatologists, dermatology providers, RNs, MAs, and ancillary staff.
UsesAndDirections.NecessaryKnowledgeExpertise: Users should have a basic understanding of dermatology and clinical practice. DermGPT is designed to be intuitive and user-friendly, but it is intended to be used as an assistant and does not replace medical care or decision-making.
UsesAndDirections.HowToUse: DermGPT can be used to look up dermatology information, answer clinical queries, look up data, answer patient questions, and access handouts. Dermatologists can ask questions in natural language and receive relevant, helpful answers. It can be accessed at www.dermgpt.com, and dermatologists can sign up for free.
UsesAndDirections.TargetedPatientPopulation: Patients seeking dermatological care, particularly those with inflammatory skin diseases.
UsesAndDirections.PatientConsentOrDisclosureRequiredOrSugg: Provides informed consent language regarding procedures and telehealth consults [SOURCE 4].

Warnings.DeveloperSuppliedWarnings: DermGPT is an AI tool and is most powerful when paired with a dermatology provider or staff who can complement its skills with their higher-level creative problem-solving. DermGPT does not replace medical care or decision-making and should not be used as a stand-alone decision maker, but as an assistant.
Warnings.ModelLimitations: The con of any AI tool is that it is not a human, nor is it trying to be. AI tools excel in efficient and data-driven tasks. They lack human creativity, intuition, and the ability to think outside the box. So, like all AI tools, DermGPT is most powerful when paired with a dermatology provider or staff who can complement its skills with their higher-level creative problem-solving. DermGPT does not replace medical care or decision-making, it should not be used as a stand-alone decision maker, but as an assistant [SOURCE 4].

TrustIngredients.AISystemFacts: DermGPT is an AI chatbot built on more than 3,000 peer-reviewed articles [SOURCE 3]. It is designed to streamline clinical tasks, improve access to dermatologic data, and save time for physicians [SOURCE 3, 4]. It assists with tasks such as prior authorizations, denial letters, board exam study, and patient education handouts [SOURCE 3, 4]. DermGPT is free for dermatologists [SOURCE 3]. It provides quick reference for medication options, dosing, and interactions; summarizes diagnosis and treatment guidelines; suggests labs, imaging, and procedures; automates documentation such as visit notes, orders, and prescriptions; writes insurance authorization letters; creates patient handouts; summarizes medical notes; assists with study guides; and provides informed consent language [SOURCE 4].

It can also be used for patient management and shared decision-making tools such as patient educational handouts and prescription programs. It can answer patient inquiries such as health online messaging and direct messaging [SOURCE 4].

UsefulnessEfficacy.GoalOfMetrics: The goal is to improve patient care and streamline dermatology practices by assisting with clinical tasks and making dermatology information readily available. It aims to save dermatologists time, allowing them to engage in more complex thinking and strengthen patient care. DermGPT also intends to provide healthcare providers with quick reference for medication options, dosing, and interactions; summarize diagnosis and treatment guidelines for complex cases; suggest appropriate labs, imaging, and procedures for diagnostic workups; automate documentation such as visit notes, orders, and prescriptions; assist with study guides for Board Exams; provide informed consent language regarding procedures and telehealth consults; write insurance authorization letters; create patient handouts regarding drugs, after-care, and more; summarize a provider’s medical notes; ask questions about diagnoses.
UsefulnessEfficacy.Interpretation: DermGPT helps improve access to dermatologic data, save time for physicians, streamline clinical tasks, and improve clinic productivity. It assists with decision-making by providing easily accessible high-quality data, patient education, research, and data analysis. The tool also helps with prior authorizations, denial letters, patient education handouts, and can draft responses to patient inquiries, thus making the process faster.
